claims.text: The FDA acarbose label says acarbose has been shown to change digoxin bioavailability when coadministered, which may require a digoxin dose adjustment.
claims.quote: Acarbose Tablets have been shown to change the bioavailability of digoxin when they are coadministered, which may require digoxin dose adjustment.

claims.text: The French acarbose label says acarbose can in some cases affect digoxin bioavailability, requiring a dose adaptation.
claims.quote: Dans certains cas, l'acarbose peut interférer sur la biodisponibilité de la digoxine, nécessitant une adaptation posologique.
claims.quoteEnglish: In some cases, acarbose can interfere with the bioavailability of digoxin, requiring a dose adjustment.

claims.text: In a randomized crossover study of healthy male volunteers, digoxin AUC and Cmax were significantly lower and tmax significantly higher after acarbose than with digoxin alone.
claims.quote: Area under the concentration-time curve (AUC0-48) and mean maximum concentration (Cmax) were significantly lower and tmax significantly increased in phases 2 and 3 compared with phase 1.

claims.text: A case report describes a 69-year-old woman whose subtherapeutic digoxin levels rose to the therapeutic range after acarbose was stopped.
claims.quote: In the absence of acarbose, the plasma concentration of digoxin increased to the therapeutic range.

headline.text: The FDA acarbose label says acarbose changes digoxin bioavailability when coadministered (c1).

reported.text: The French label also reports acarbose can interfere with digoxin bioavailability (c2).
A randomized crossover study in healthy volunteers found lower digoxin exposure after acarbose (c3). A case report describes subtherapeutic digoxin levels (c4).

gaps.text: The controlled study was in healthy male volunteers and measured digoxin concentrations, not clinical outcomes.
